text:
{
  "background_info": "Student Name: Ravi Nair
Age / Grade: 9 years / Grade 3
School: VIBGYOR High, Pune
IEP Meeting Date: 19 October 2026
Services Begin Date: 2 November 2026
Disability Classification: Autism Spectrum Disorder (mild) under RPwD Act 2016
Dominant Language: English / Hindi
Parent/Guardian Contact: Mr. & Mrs. Nair (Contact via School Portal)
Medical Alerts: Auditory sensory hypersensitivity; no known pharmacological alerts.",

  "academic_performance": "Present Level: Academic/Educational Achievement - Ravi Nair is currently functioning above grade level in Mathematics and Science, demonstrating exceptional memory for recalling factual information and advanced problem-solving skills. He functions at grade level in English reading comprehension, while Social Studies performance is impacted by complex narrative structures.
Present Level: Cognitive Ability - Ravi demonstrates superior non-verbal reasoning and factual retention skills, exceeding grade-level expectations in logical analysis and structured academic tasks.
Present Level: Language Ability - Ravi displays strong functional vocabulary and effective one-on-one communication skills with teachers and familiar peers, though pragmatics in group conversations require structured guidance.
Present Level: Learning Style - Ravi is a visual and structured learner who benefits significantly from predictable routines, clear schedules, visual prompts, and task-oriented instructions due to Autism Spectrum Disorder.
Present Level: Rate of Progress - Ravi demonstrates rapid academic acquisition in structured contexts, maintaining a stable above-average trajectory in core academic subjects.",

  "social_development": "Present Level: Peer and Adult Relationships - Ravi Nair communicates effectively in one-on-one interactions with teachers and peers. However, he experiences difficulty navigating unstructured activities such as recess and lunch, frequently leading to social isolation.
Present Level: Social Adjustment and Self-Concept - Ravi displays confidence in academic settings, particularly in science and math. Unstructured social settings and sensory overload heighten his anxiety and self-consciousness.
Present Level: Behaviors Impeding Learning - Unannounced modifications to daily routines and elevated environmental noise trigger anxiety, emotional distress, and behavioral dysregulation. Proactive visual schedules and structured transition notifications are required to maintain emotional regulation.",

  "physical_development": "Present Level: Motor Development - Ravi Nair demonstrates age-appropriate fine and gross motor skills required for grade-level classroom tasks and physical education activities.
Present Level: Sensory Development - Ravi displays sensory over-responsivity to environmental noise (auditory hypersensitivity), causing acute distress during assemblies, cafeteria time, and noisy classroom transitions, directly related to his diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (mild).
Present Level: Health and Vitality - Ravi maintains good general health, physical stamina, and regular school attendance, with no physical or medical limitations reported.",

  "management_needs": "Ravi Nair requires a moderate level of environmental modifications and specialized human/material supports to ensure full access to the educational curriculum.
Environmental management requires a highly structured, predictable classroom environment, visual daily schedules, advance transition warnings, noise-canceling headphones, and a designated quiet workspace for sensory regulation.
Human and material management includes access to speech and language therapy, social skills training, adult-facilitated peer activities during unstructured times, and regular teacher training on Autism support strategies per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.39).",

  "long_term_outcomes": "N/A — Student is below 14 years. Long-term adult outcomes and transition planning will be developed at age 14 per RPwD Act 2016 and NCTE Guidelines.",

  "annual_goals": "Annual Goal: Ravi will independently navigate daily routine transitions across classroom settings without behavioral distress by 31 March 2027.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Ravi will independently transition between classroom activities using a visual schedule without emotional outbursts in 4 out of 5 trials across 3 consecutive weeks as measured by teacher observation logs.
2. By the end of Term 2, Ravi will transition to unannounced schedule changes using visual advance notifications in 4 out of 5 observed instances as measured by teacher observation logs.
3. By the end of Term 3, Ravi will independently manage all daily activity transitions using his personal visual checklist with 90% accuracy as measured by teacher observation logs.
Evaluation Procedures: Teacher observation logs, behavioral checklists
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal: Ravi will initiate and maintain a two-turn reciprocal social interaction with a peer during unstructured school periods by 31 March 2027.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Ravi will participate in one structured, adult-facilitated peer cooperative activity during recess twice a week in 4 out of 5 opportunities as measured by playground observation checklists.
2. By the end of Term 2, Ravi will participate in an interest-based lunch club and initiate a greeting to a peer in 3 out of 5 observed opportunities as measured by counselor tracking sheets.
3. By the end of Term 3, Ravi will successfully initiate conversation and maintain a two-turn reciprocal interaction with a peer during unstructured periods in at least 4 out of 5 recorded opportunities as measured by weekly counselor and teacher tracking sheets.
Evaluation Procedures: Peer interaction tracking sheets, playground observation checklists, counselor notes
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal: Ravi will independently utilize sensory regulation strategies during high-noise classroom activities to maintain task engagement by 31 March 2027.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Ravi will independently request and use noise-canceling headphones when auditory noise causes discomfort in 4 out of 5 instances as measured by teacher tracking logs.
2. By the end of Term 2, Ravi will independently access his designated quiet work space when experiencing sensory distress and return to class tasks within 10 minutes in 4 out of 5 trials as measured by behavioral logs.
3. By the end of Term 3, Ravi will self-regulate during noisy group environments using his sensory accommodations to maintain task engagement for 80% of activity time as measured by teacher observation logs.
Evaluation Procedures: Self-monitoring charts, teacher tracking logs, sensory observation records
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly",

  "special_education_services": "A. Special Education Programs and Services:
- Resource Room Support: 3 sessions per week (45 minutes per session), beginning 2 November 2026 through 31 March 2027.
- Speech and Language Therapy: 2 sessions per week (30 minutes per session), beginning 2 November 2026 through 31 March 2027 per RPwD Act Section 17(a) and NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30).
- Social Skills Training (individual or group): 2 sessions per week (45 minutes per session), beginning 2 November 2026 through 31 March 2027 per RPwD Act Section 16(iv).

B. Extended School Year Services:
No. Extended school year services are not required as Ravi demonstrates stable retention of learned skills.

C. Supplementary Aids and Modifications:
- Structured, predictable classroom environment with visual schedules.
- Sensory accommodation plan including noise-canceling headphones and designated quiet work space for auditory sensory regulation per RPwD Act Section 16(iii).
- Visual schedules and structured advance notifications for routine transitions per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30).
- Adult-facilitated peer cooperative activities and structured lunch/recess interest groups per RPwD Act Section 16(iv).
- Behavioural support plan to assist with anxiety management during unexpected routine changes.

D. Assistive Technology Devices and Services:
- Noise-canceling headphones for auditory sensory regulation in noisy classroom and non-academic environments per RPwD Act Section 16(iii).
- Individual desktop visual schedules and visual transition timers.

E. Program Modifications for School Personnel:
- Capacity building and teacher training on Autism Spectrum Disorder, sensory regulation strategies, and UDL-based differentiated teaching per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30 & p.39).
- Bi-weekly consultation between special educator, speech therapist, and general education team.

F. Individual Testing Modifications:
- Extended time on assessments (minimum 25% extra time) per RPwD Act Section 17.
- Separate room for assessments to minimize auditory and visual distractions per RPwD Act Section 17.
- Visual and explicit verbal instructions during testing sessions.",

  "general_education_participation": "Ravi Nair will participate in general education classes for approximately 85% of the school day, including Mathematics, Science, English, Social Studies, Art, Music, and Physical Education. He will receive pull-out specialized support for speech and language therapy and social skills training during non-core activity periods. No exemption from second language or mainstream subjects is requested or granted, as Ravi performs strongly academically and benefits from universal design for learning (UDL) whole-class instruction per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30).",

  "participating_agencies": "N/A — Transition services not yet applicable. Will be identified at age 14.",

  "coordinated_activities": "1. Instruction: Special education resource support and UDL-based differentiated instruction in general classroom per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines.
2. Related Services: Speech and language therapy, social skills training, and sensory regulation accommodations.
3. Employment/Post-secondary Education: N/A at age 9.
4. Community Experience: N/A at age 9.
5. Activities of Daily Living: Self-regulation, managing daily visual schedules, and independent transition routines.
6. Functional Vocational Assessment: N/A at age 9.",

  "graduation_info": "Certificate sought: CBSE Primary Completion Certificate leading to Secondary School Certificate. Expected year of school completion: 2036. Board examination provisions will include extended time (minimum 25%) and a separate assessment room per RPwD Act accommodations. Consistent with Sections 6 and 7, no second language exemption is required or granted.",

  "recommendations_summary": "Disability Classification: Autism Spectrum Disorder (mild) per RPwD Act 2016 Schedule.
Recommended Placement: General education classroom at VIBGYOR High, Pune, with integrated resource room support, speech and language therapy, and social skills group interventions per RPwD Act Section 16(iv).
Extended School Year Services: No.
Transportation Needs: Standard school bus transport with designated quiet seating.
Annual IEP Review Date: 19 October 2027.",

  "progress_reporting": "Progress reporting to parents will occur on a quarterly basis, aligning with the regular report card schedule for non-disabled peers. Reporting methods will include formal written progress reports evaluating short-term objectives using numeric criteria, teacher observation logs, and quarterly parent-teacher IEP review conferences."
}
